name: Argentina
genZNote: Argentina stretches so far south that Ushuaia, its southernmost city, calls itself 'the End of the World' — the country spans nearly the entire length of South America, from subtropical north to Patagonian glaciers and the edge of Antarctica.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: The second-largest country in South America by area, stretching from subtropical regions in the north to the sub-Antarctic Tierra del Fuego in the far south.
Home to the vast Pampas grasslands (a globally significant agricultural region), the Andes mountains along its western border with Chile, and Patagonia's glaciers and steppes in the south.
Ushuaia, its southernmost major city, is often called 'the End of the World' and serves as a gateway for Antarctic expeditions.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Spanish is the official language; the culture reflects strong European (particularly Italian and Spanish) immigrant influence alongside indigenous heritage.
The birthplace of tango music and dance, which originated in Buenos Aires and became a globally recognised cultural export.
Football holds deep cultural significance, with Argentina among the most successful national teams in World Cup history, and figures like Diego Maradona and Lionel Messi as global icons.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A federal presidential republic composed of 23 provinces and an autonomous capital city (Buenos Aires), modelled significantly on the US constitutional structure.
Experienced periods of military dictatorship, notably 1976-1983, followed by a return to sustained democratic governance.
Has faced repeated economic crises and high inflation over recent decades, a persistent challenge for governance and policy.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: Has produced multiple Nobel laureates in science, including in physiology/medicine and chemistry, reflecting a strong scientific research tradition.
A major centre for nuclear energy research and technology in Latin America, with an advanced civilian nuclear power programme.
Strong biotechnology and agricultural science base, supporting its position as a major global grain and soy exporter.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A G20 member and a founding member of Mercosur, the South American regional trade bloc.
Maintains a long-standing sovereignty dispute with the United Kingdom over the Falkland Islands (Islas Malvinas), including the 1982 Falklands War.
An active participant in Antarctic research and governance, given its geographic proximity and territorial claims in the region.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Argentina share warm relations, with cooperation growing in agriculture, pharmaceuticals, and lithium/critical mineral supply (Argentina holds significant lithium reserves).
Argentina is an important source of edible oils (soybean oil) for India, a significant trade relationship.
Both countries collaborate on nuclear energy cooperation and space research, alongside growing investment ties.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A major global exporter of soybeans, beef, wheat, and other agricultural products from its fertile Pampas region.
Holds significant lithium reserves as part of South America's 'lithium triangle', a resource of growing global strategic importance for battery technology.
Has experienced chronic high inflation and periodic sovereign debt crises, significant recurring economic policy challenges.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Tango music and dance, originating in Buenos Aires.
Football greatness, including World Cup titles and icons like Maradona and Messi.
The Pampas grasslands and being a major global grain/beef exporter.
Patagonia's dramatic glaciers and landscapes.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Argentine Peso (ARS), issued by the Central Bank of Argentina (BCRA).
Economy centred on agriculture — a major global exporter of soybeans, corn, wheat, and beef.
Has experienced repeated episodes of high inflation and currency instability over recent decades.
Wine (notably Malbec) and lithium (part of South America's 'lithium triangle') are growing export sectors.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Spans dramatic ecological extremes: the Pampas grasslands, Patagonian steppe and glaciers, and subtropical wetlands in the north.
Co-hosts Iguazú Falls with Brazil, one of the world's largest waterfall systems and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Los Glaciares National Park protects the Perito Moreno Glacier, one of the few advancing glaciers in the world.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Colonized by Spain; declared independence in 1816.
20th century marked by recurring military coups, including the 1976-1983 military dictatorship and its 'Dirty War' of state repression.
Fought the Falklands/Malvinas War with the United Kingdom in 1982 over the disputed South Atlantic islands.
Returned to civilian democratic rule in 1983, which has continued since.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1853 Constitution established a federal republic, modelled partly on the US Constitution.
1994 constitutional reform allowed presidential re-election and granted Buenos Aires city autonomous status.
Transition from military dictatorship back to democracy in 1983 remains a key modern turning point.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: CONAE (Comisión Nacional de Actividades Espaciales) runs Argentina's satellite programme, including the SAOCOM Earth-observation satellites.
Strong biotechnology and agri-tech sector, including early adoption of genetically modified crop technology.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Football is a national passion — three-time FIFA World Cup champions (1978, 1986, 2022), home to Diego Maradona and Lionel Messi.
Tango originated in Buenos Aires and is recognised by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage.
Jorge Luis Borges is one of the most influential writers in Spanish-language literature.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of Mercosur (South American trade bloc) and the Organization of American States (OAS).
Member of the UN and the G20; not a permanent UN Security Council member.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Argentina is a federal presidential republic in South America, home to tango and world-class football, a major agricultural exporter facing recurring economic challenges.
keyFacts: Capital: Buenos Aires. Currency: Argentine Peso.
Federal presidential republic; 23 provinces plus the autonomous capital.
Birthplace of tango; multiple football World Cup titles.
Holds major lithium reserves as part of South America's 'lithium triangle'.
commonConfusion: The Falkland Islands (Islas Malvinas) dispute is with the United Kingdom, not with a South American neighbour — it led to the 1982 Falklands War.

highYieldFacts: Argentina: federal presidential republic, capital Buenos Aires, birthplace of tango.
Major soybean/beef exporter; holds significant lithium reserves (lithium triangle).
India-Argentina: growing trade in edible oils and lithium/critical minerals; nuclear energy cooperation.
commonTraps: Confusing the Falklands/Malvinas dispute (Argentina vs UK) with a dispute involving a South American neighbour.
Assuming Argentina's economic struggles reflect all of South America — its chronic inflation is a distinctive national challenge.
mustRemember: Argentina: tango/football culture, Pampas agri-exporter, lithium triangle member, growing India trade in oils/minerals.
